review_kind: statement and written-proof-method correspondence, with complete matching human-readable proofs

category_definitions.same_argument: The written argument and formal proof have the same substantive steps; explicit carrier, metric, measurability or algebra bookkeeping does not change the route.
category_definitions.expanded_argument: The source states or cites a compressed step; Lean proves the same mathematical mechanism in greater detail.
category_definitions.alternative_argument: At least one substantive step uses a different proof route; a complete human-readable proof matching Lean is supplied.
category_definitions.no_separate_proof: The source makes a direct observation without a separate proof environment; Lean supplies its elementary proof.

entries.title: Exponential empirical-law concentration
entries.source_revision_change: Mathematical conclusion retained; updated source locations and proof-method comparison bind this review to the current F6E3BB4D manuscript.
entries.written_argument: Use the actual conditional Laplace limit, Markov height and centered floor-mgf bounds, Stone-Weierstrass density of Lipschitz cube tests, the normal-CDF Lipschitz bound and Cauchy-Schwarz square-root height transfer; finish with finite weak tests and continuity-set Portmanteau.
entries.lean_argument: The actual compact-metric Lipschitz sublattice contains constants, is closed under minimum and maximum, and strongly separates pairs by an affine distance function. The proved lattice Stone-Weierstrass theorem gives uniform approximation. Coordinate clamping extends the approximant to a globally bounded ambient Lipschitz function. The production concentration call uses that producer and the written Cauchy-Schwarz estimate.
entries.precise_method_comparison: The revised Stone-Weierstrass/Lipschitz route is now the actual production proof. Lean supplies the explicit Lipschitz sublattice, its strong two-point separation, and the one-Lipschitz clamp extension. The earlier finite Kuhn interpolation is supplementary. Absolute two-sided test estimates also imply the source one-sided finite-test estimates. Lean carries out the probability-logarithm step as direct exponential Markov bounds, including zero-probability events; the written logarithmic bound uses the usual extended-real convention log(0)=-infinity.
entries.recommended_annotation: The statement is fully Lean-verified. The formal proof follows the written argument with its finite triangulation and probability steps expanded; a complete matching proof is supplied at leanproof:ANT-2-1.
entries.scope_note: The paper concludes continuity-set frequencies converge in probability. Lean proves the stronger fixed-tolerance exponential tail; this does not claim a fluctuation scale or a large-deviation rate function.
entries.comparison: The revised Stone-Weierstrass/Lipschitz route is now the actual production proof. Lean supplies the explicit Lipschitz sublattice, its strong two-point separation, and the one-Lipschitz clamp extension. The earlier finite Kuhn interpolation is supplementary. Absolute two-sided test estimates also imply the source one-sided finite-test estimates. Lean carries out the probability-logarithm step as direct exponential Markov bounds, including zero-probability events; the written logarithmic bound uses the usual extended-real convention log(0)=-infinity.
